newsitem.title: USA: NYPA seeks to halt NIMO transmission plan.
newsitem.headline: NYPA seeks to halt NIMO transmission plan.

text.p: The New York Power Authority (NYPA) said Thursday it is seeking a federal order to stop Niagara Mohawk Power Corp (NIMO) from cutting transmission service to NYPA's upstate New York customers.

Niagara Mohawk's "ultimate goal is to deny transmission service to existing and prospective NYPA customers in order to serve these customers itself," NYPA said its filing with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC).
The NYPA customers are considered attractive because of their high energy usage.
NYPA alleged NIMO's move is anti-competitive and denies those customers access to power from NYPA which is cheaper than NIMO's.
The state-owned utility contends up to 8,000 jobs at 37 New York companies served by NYPA could be eliminated by NIMO's refusal to continue carrying its electricity.
NYPA's complaint stemmed from NIMO's refusal to deliver power over its lines to Cascades Niagara Falls Inc, which manufactures recycled paper products.
NYPA agreed to supply electricity to Cascades under a 10-year, 12,000-kilowatt contract, beginning March 1.

Besides threatening to curtail transmission service, NIMO announced Tuesday it will cancel most power deliveries from NYPA's 832 megawatt (MW) Fitzpatrick nuclear power plant to NYPA customers within its service territory from May 24.
NIMO is "using uncertainty about future transmission service as a lever to induce NYPA customers to switch their service to Niagara Mowhawk," NYPA said.
To improve its prospects in a deregulated marketplace, NIMO is trying to buy out or rid itself of what it considers uneconomical contracts with NYPA and independent power producers.
